game.name: Tiny Rogues
game.short_description: Tiny Rogues is a challenging fantasy rogue-lite bullet-hell dungeon crawler with rpg elements. Build a new unique character each run and fight one monster-infested room after another! Discover unique weapons, collect magical items and level up to become more and more powerful!

commentary.label: Tier list Part 1 (2023)
commentary.summary: Tiny Rogues is a cute pixel-art top-down action roguelike with bullet-hell elements. He sees it as simple and straightforward, not trying to be unique, but doing the basics very well for a cheap small game. Level-ups give impactful abilities, and many characters and weapons keep runs varied. He calls it a good game that surprised him with its fun and content, and places it in high B tier.
praise: Level-up abilities are impactful, so each run feels distinct
Many characters, abilities and weapons give lots of customization
Lots of bosses, and boss fights are the highlight
Surprising amount of content for a small, cheap game
Successfully delivers an old-school approach in a new game
criticism: Minimalistic gameplay means runs feel similar over a long time (e.g. 50 hours) despite the customization
unique_points: Deliberately not unique; succeeds by executing a simple, straightforward formula well
Impactful level-up picks create run variety even with minimal core gameplay
design_criteria: Run variety: impactful level-up abilities make runs feel different
Character/weapon diversity: many options for customization
Level design: no level variety is a weakness
Enemy design: repetitive, but many bosses
Boss design: fights are the highlight
Content value: lots of content for a small cheap game
Longevity: minimalistic gameplay limits feel of difference over 50 hours

commentary.label: Tier list Part 2 (2024)
commentary.summary: Tiny Rogues is a simple top-down dungeon crawler roguelike that he previously rated in an earlier tier list. A huge content update transformed it, adding a large amount of weapons, builds, characters, secrets, bosses and a full meta-progression layer. He loves the expanded game but notes it is now less approachable because items and keywords carry much more text and stats. He still recommends it, including to newcomers to the genre, and moves it up from B to A, placing it above Atomic Crops.
praise: Enormous amount of content added in a single update
Huge variety of weapons, builds, characters, secrets and bosses
Meta progression added that makes it feel like a new experience
Core mechanics remain simple and easy to pick up
Still very approachable and recommended for people new to roguelikes
Items and classes are very different from one another
criticism: Items became complicated with many new keywords and lots of text
More stats to track than before, which raises the learning curve
Understanding the different builds takes more time
No longer as approachable as the original simple version, and can be intimidating at first
unique_points: Mechanically simple top-down crawler layered with deep item and build complexity
A major update fundamentally reshaped the game and changed his opinion of it
Item text and keywords are secondary to gameplay; players pick them up over time
commentary.quote: I'm going to bump up its rating from a b to a solid a tier
design_criteria: Content volume: weapons, builds, characters, secrets and bosses add replay value
Meta-progression: newly added system gives long-term goals
Simplicity and approachability: core mechanics stay simple but item text raises the barrier
Build diversity: classes and items differ greatly from each other
Complexity of stats and keywords: a growing number of stats and keywords can overwhelm new players
commentary.rerank_note: Previously discussed on the last tier list and rated B; after a huge content update he moves it up to A tier, placed above Atomic Crops.

community.one_liner: A solo-developed (RubyDev) pixel-art action rogue-lite with bullet-hell combat, RPG-style stats and an enormous pool of weapons, equipment and traits, played in roughly 30-minute runs down 20+ floors.
community.consensus_summary: Players love it: Steam shows Overwhelmingly Positive (about 96 percent of roughly 10,800 reviews), and many reviewers call it one of their favourite roguelites, praising build depth and value at $9.99. Metacritic has a page but no critic or user reviews, and no OpenCritic entry was found, so critic coverage is essentially absent and reception is almost entirely community-driven. The game is still in Early Access after launching in September 2022. The last big content update was around late 2023, which produced a steady stream of 'is it abandoned?' complaints, though the developer posts monthly devblogs through 2026 and is doing a near-total rewrite (new hub, dual wielding, consumable rework, mid-run saving, localization promised). The most repeated practical complaints are no mid-run save, late-floor screen clarity, and occasional freezes.
best_things: Extreme build variety: hundreds of weapons, 500+ equipment items and 100+ traits combine into 'fireworks' synergies, and many reviewers say learning them is the core joy
Snappy, smooth combat and dodging with a strong 'one more run' loop; a run takes about 30 minutes, which busy players like
Price-to-content ratio: repeatedly described as underpriced ('price of a fast food meal') for the amount of content
Large roster of unlockable classes (34 per the store page) that change playstyle, with unlocks that keep coming without watering down the game
Responsive, passionate solo developer with human, transparent devblogs; several reviewers cite this as a reason to recommend
Easy to learn controls with deep, complex systems underneath; compared favourably to Binding of Isaac, Hades, Enter the Gungeon and Nuclear Throne
Optional difficulty scaling (Cinder system) and optional progression, so the game stays fun without forced grinding
Pixel-art charm, a catchy soundtrack and memorable boss personalities that reviewers say give the game heart despite simple graphics
worst_things: No mid-run save or pause-and-resume: runs can last 1-1.5 hours and players with jobs or kids find this a dealbreaker; it is the single most repeated complaint
Long stagnation in Early Access: reviewers say no meaningful content update since late 2023, leading to 'abandoned' and 'dead game' talk (a 44-comment Steam thread) despite ongoing devblogs
Screen clarity on later floors: bullet-hell density and effects make it hard to see what is happening, leading to 'spray and pray' play
Stability: several reviewers report hard freezes mid-boss or at floor transitions 30+ minutes into a run, plus a controller-detection bug with Wooting keyboards
Weak onboarding: most content is unlocked by default with little explanation, and the Alignment mechanic required to progress past floors 10-11 is not explained
Some classes feel too similar (ranged DPS with small gimmicks), undercutting the headline class count
No official Chinese (or other) localization despite being requested for years; promised for the rewrite
Some boss fights are very short (seconds) or, conversely, specific bosses like the Jousting Champion are called un-fun
improvements: Add a mid-run save/suspend function (promised in the 2026 rewrite announcement)
Ship the long-delayed big update with real new content and endgame progression, and give a clearer release timeline
Improve visual clarity on late floors (readability of projectiles and effects)
Add endgame or post-unlock progression: one reviewer was stuck after unlocking the first 16 characters, and there are requests for an endless mode
Better tutorialisation of mechanics such as Alignment, keywords and trait interactions
Make classes and early-unlock characters more mechanically distinct; fix freezes and input bugs; add localization
unique_things: Generates a new 'character' each run by combining class, weapons, armor, traits and consumables, closer to an RPG loadout than a fixed character
Bullet-hell dodging mixed with stat-driven, dungeon-crawler build-crafting; tagged as a blend of Isaac-style item synergy with Nuclear Throne-like speed
Extremely fast rooms and bosses when the build works: several reviewers say encounters are a 'test' of whether you understood the systems
Sheer content scale for a solo dev: 40+ bosses, 400+ weapons, 20+ themed floors, random events and NPCs
Planned rewrite introduces a Rogue Hideout hub for informed floor selection, dual wielding instead of weapon swap, and PoE-style crafting orbs and scrolls
tedious_or_disliked: Early floors (first ten) are too easy for experienced players, so they go on autopilot for about 40 minutes before real difficulty starts
Floor 10 onward is a sharp difficulty spike with bullet-heavy chaos that some players cannot get past, blocking character unlocks
Long, unskippable animations (for example the loot sequence after floor bosses)
Trait and loot selection RNG and the need to reroll around starter items; choices tend to repeat across runs
Grind to unlock later characters feels samey for some, and playstyles run out of steam
Keyword and effect overload makes builds feel hard to parse
divisive_points: Complexity: praised as deep build-crafting by fans, but called both 'too simple and too complex' and keyword soup by critics
Difficulty curve: some find it too easy early and brutal late, others say it is never unfair
Passive versus active feel: a few reviewers feel build effects are passive (enemies burn) so the game feels closer to an autobattler than Noita or Roboquest, while fans praise the combos
The upcoming rewrite: fans are excited, while some worry that adding pillars and pitfalls could break the rhythmic looping movement feel they currently love
community.reception_notes: Launched in Early Access on Sep 23, 2022 at $9.99 (Windows only, no Mac/Linux) and built its audience through word of mouth; the developer stated the game would get pricier with each major expansion. The original plan was to leave Early Access around December 2024 or later, which has slipped. Content updates slowed after late 2023, the community's main frustration. In Feb 2026 the developer announced a full rewrite with a 67-page design doc, promising localization, mid-run saving, performance gains and modding support; devblogs from March to September 2026 show the rewrite largely done and content production in progress, with a new programmer and artist joining and a delay from the developer's gallbladder surgery in June 2026. No date for the big update was found. Note: web search was unavailable (budget exhausted), so no professional press reviews were found; Metacritic's page exists but has zero reviews, and OpenCritic could not be confirmed.
